Szatmarcseke Jewish Cemetery 1

Jewish Cemetery · Szatmárcseke, Hungary

Not demolished. Jews settled in Szatmárcseke in the second half of the 18th century; population grew from 59 (1840) to 114 by 1880, declining to 68 by 1941. The community maintained a mikveh, kosher butcher, and charity organization, joining the Orthodox stream in 1876; its synagogue was consecrated in 1884. By 1941, young men were conscripted for forced labor; following the 1944 occupation, residents were funneled through the local ghetto, then Kölcse and Mátészalka ghettos, before deportation to Auschwitz - about 70 were murdered according to Yad Vashem records. This cemetery's oldest tombstone dates to 1840, its newest to 1939.
